basis: Prepared from a paragraph-level extraction of 49 CFR 391.2, Part 391 Subpart G (391.61-391.69), 391.1, 383.3 and 382.103 at eCFR issue 2026-10-05. Not read: 390.3T(f), Part 381, FMCSA guidance. This is a draft for an administrator to review against the official text; it has not been approved.

wording.title: Review the claimed exemption and confirm which rules it actually covers
wording.purpose: An exemption from one part of the regulations does not carry over to another. FleetComply does not apply exemptions automatically.
wording.applicability: Shown where the user indicated an exemption may apply. Whether the driver and the operation qualify is decided from their own facts and records, not by this step.
requiredAction: Identify the exact exemption or exception being claimed and the section it comes from, and keep a copy of any FMCSA exemption notice or waiver.

Check which requirements that section relieves. The exceptions and limited exemptions in Part 391 (§ 391.2 and Subpart G, §§ 391.61–391.69) relieve specific driver-qualification requirements for the drivers they describe — for example applications, background investigations and road tests for certain long-standing single-employer drivers, or the application and investigation steps for multiple-employer drivers. Nothing in Subpart G exempts a driver from holding a commercial driver’s license.

For the CDL itself, look only to § 383.3. It excepts certain military drivers and drivers of covered farm vehicles, and it lets a State choose to waive the CDL requirement for farmers, firefighters and emergency vehicle drivers and certain snow and ice removal drivers, or to issue restricted CDLs for certain industries. The general exceptions in § 390.3(f) do not apply to the CDL rules unless § 383.3 says so (§ 383.3(b)).
If the exception depends on a State’s choice, confirm with that State’s licensing agency that the State has adopted it and that it applies where the driver will operate.
Confirm the driver and the operation meet every condition of the section relied on, and write down the facts that show it.

Drug and alcohol testing follows the CDL rules, not Part 391. Part 382 applies to drivers who are subject to the CDL requirements of Part 383 (§ 382.103(a)), and its only exceptions are the ones listed in § 382.103(d): employers covered solely by the transit testing rules of Part 655, military drivers a State must waive from Part 383, farmers and emergency vehicle operators a State has chosen to exempt from Part 383, and covered farm vehicles. The general exceptions in § 390.3T(f) do not apply to testing (§ 382.103(c)). A driver-qualification exemption under Part 391 does not change whether testing applies.

Have a qualified reviewer decide which checklist items the exemption affects. Mark only those items Not Applicable, each with the section as the reason. Do not mark CDL items or drug and alcohol testing items Not Applicable on the strength of a Part 391 exemption.
documentation: The section relied on, and any FMCSA exemption notice or waiver
The facts showing each condition of the exemption is met (for example dates of continuous employment, type of operation, vehicle, distance from the farm)
For a State-discretion CDL waiver: confirmation that the State has adopted it
Reviewer’s written determination listing each checklist item affected and why
wording.exceptions: Not read for this entry, so confirm from the official text before relying on them: the general exceptions in § 390.3T(f); waivers and exemptions granted under Part 381; and FMCSA guidance. Two points are left open for the reviewer: § 383.3(d) lets a State waive the CDL for certain snow and ice removal drivers, but § 382.103(d) does not list them among the testing exceptions; and whether a given State has adopted any discretionary waiver is not something this guide knows.
wording.verification: The reviewer’s determination names the section, the conditions met and each item affected, and is signed and dated.
